_readme: Labelled query -> gold source pairs for the retrieval benchmark.
Each `query` is a sentence of the kind a researcher might write and then want to
cite. Queries deliberately PARAPHRASE the paper's contribution rather than quote
its abstract: copying abstract wording would make retrieval a lexical-overlap test
rather than a semantic one, and would flatter any embedding model.
`gold` is the arXiv id in corpus.json that a correct system should return first.
Caveat, stated plainly: this is a PROXY for real citation behaviour. Real citation
contexts are messier, often cite several works at once, and frequently cite for
method rather than for a headline claim. The corpus is also topically clustered
(mostly deep learning), which is deliberate — semantically adjacent papers make
discrimination HARDER than a corpus drawn from unrelated fields would.

queries.query: Replacing recurrence entirely with self-attention allows sequence models to be trained with far more parallelism.
Scaled dot-product attention computed over multiple heads lets a model attend to information from different representation subspaces at once.
Conditioning a language representation on both left and right context simultaneously during pre-training improves downstream sentence-level tasks.
Masking a fraction of input tokens and predicting them is an effective pre-training objective for bidirectional encoders.
Adding identity shortcut connections makes it practical to optimise networks that are hundreds of layers deep.
Framing the layers as learning a residual function relative to the input eases the degradation problem in very deep vision models.
Training a generator against a discriminator in a minimax game lets a model learn to synthesise realistic samples without an explicit likelihood.
Adapting the learning rate per parameter using running estimates of the first and second gradient moments works well for noisy objectives.
Stacking many small convolutional filters instead of fewer large ones improves large-scale image classification accuracy.
Sufficiently large autoregressive language models can perform new tasks from a handful of demonstrations in the prompt, without gradient updates.
Careful tuning of pre-training hyperparameters and training for longer on more data substantially improves an existing masked language model.
Splitting an image into fixed-size patches and feeding them to a standard transformer encoder is competitive with convolutional architectures at scale.
A smaller network can be trained to match the softened output distribution of a larger one, transferring much of its generalisation ability.
A siamese encoder fine-tuned with a similarity objective produces sentence vectors that can be compared with cosine distance efficiently.
Learned dense embeddings for questions and passages can outperform sparse term-matching retrieval for open-domain question answering.
Combining a parametric generator with a non-parametric document index lets a model ground its outputs in retrieved evidence.
A dimension-reduction technique grounded in manifold theory can preserve more global structure than t-SNE while scaling better.
Word vectors that vary with sentence context capture syntax and polysemy better than a single fixed vector per word type.
Shallow log-linear architectures can learn useful word vectors from very large corpora at a fraction of the training cost.
Vector arithmetic over learned word representations captures analogical relationships between words.
A first-order approximation of spectral convolutions lets neural networks classify nodes directly on graph-structured data.
Normalising across the features of a single training example rather than across the batch suits recurrent architectures better.
Normalising layer inputs using minibatch statistics permits much higher learning rates and reduces sensitivity to initialisation.
A new boson with a mass near 125 GeV was observed in proton-proton collisions, consistent with the predicted Standard Model scalar.
The diphoton and four-lepton decay channels together yielded a local significance above five standard deviations.
